findings.current: Was it when I achieved Great Completion in the Jin Family's Manoeuvre Technique? Or the Jin Family's Spear Technique?
findings.defect: “Manoeuvre” uses British spelling despite the requirement for contemporary US English.
findings.rationale: The established technique name should use consistent US-English spelling throughout the reading copy.
findings.replacement: Was it when I achieved Great Completion in the Jin Family's Maneuver Technique? Or the Jin Family's Spear Technique?

findings.current: Circulating my own qi would be one thing, but if I let go of control here, I could easily suffer an Internal Injury.
findings.defect: The generic condition “internal injury” is unnecessarily capitalized as though it were a formal System term.
findings.rationale: Lowercase matches ordinary prose usage and avoids introducing an unestablished formal term.
findings.replacement: Circulating my own qi would be one thing, but if I let go of control here, I could easily suffer an internal injury.
findings.source: Chapter 292, opening narration after the Quest prompt

findings.current: Before sunset, all four had succeeded in completing a complete circulation.
findings.defect: “Completing a complete circulation” is conspicuously repetitive and awkward.
findings.rationale: The replacement retains the established term “complete circulation” while removing the accidental repetition.
findings.replacement: Before sunset, all four had completed one complete circulation.

findings.current: But the person who showed the most unexpected performance was someone else.
findings.defect: “Showed the most unexpected performance” is an unnatural English collocation that weakens Taekyung's conversational narration.
findings.rationale: The replacement conveys the same transition naturally and fits the brisk first-person voice.
findings.replacement: But someone else was the biggest surprise.

findings.current: I asked a Senior who joined earlier than me, and he told me to sleep as much as I could on the way there.
findings.defect: Capitalized “Senior” reads like a literalized Korean workplace title rather than natural contemporary US English.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the employment seniority relationship without introducing a stiff, unestablished title.
findings.replacement: I asked someone who joined before me, and he told me to sleep as much as I could on the way there.

findings.current: Two more mutated Gate accidents occurred, and a post that attracted a great deal of attention appeared on a Hunter community site.
findings.defect: “Mutated Gate” is treated elsewhere in the packet as the established name of the phenomenon, but “mutated” is lowercased here.
findings.rationale: Capitalization should remain consistent for the established Gate phenomenon.
findings.replacement: Two more Mutated Gate accidents occurred, and a post that attracted a great deal of attention appeared on a Hunter community site.

findings.current: He had a certain amount of leadership and excellent combat ability, so whenever we raided together, he acted as my hands and feet.
findings.defect: “Had a certain amount of leadership” and “acted as my hands and feet” are stiff Korean-influenced constructions that drift from Taekyung's natural narrative voice.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves Jinsoo's operational role while using natural, concise contemporary English consistent with the checkpoint summary.
findings.replacement: He had decent leadership skills and excellent combat ability, so whenever we raided together, he served as my right hand.

summary: The packet is coherent and preserves its active hooks without accidental spoilers or internal contradictions. Eight minor corrections are actionable: two US-English spelling inconsistencies, one capitalization drift, one terminology-capitalization drift, and four awkward or calqued constructions.
